newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia amending law to protect domestic workers.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia amending law to protect domestic workers.

text.p: Malaysia will amend its employment laws to enable it to prosecute employers who sack Malaysian workers and replace them with foreigners, the national Bernama news agency reported on Friday.

"The matter is serious. Some of the affected workers met me to report on it and most of the cases occurred in the manufacturing sector," Human Resources Minister Lim Ah Lek was quoted by Bernama as saying.
Lim said the government would amend the Employment Act 1955 and pending the change, Malaysia would revoke the work permits of foreigners working for employers who recruited them to replace locals.
Several cases in the Kuala Lumpur area were being investigated, he said.
Labour-starved Malaysia, with a population of about 21 million, has an estimated two million foreigners working for lower wages, half of them illegal.
The government has given the illegal immigrants until the end of this month to register or face deportation. Authorities had earlier set a December 31, 1996, deadline to register.
So far, more than 960,000 illegal workers have registered.
Since announcing the registration campaign, Malaysia has launched a nationwide operation to round up illegal workers, including going house-to-house to check on maids' working papers.
